title: Typosquatted npm packages deliver an infostealer
text: Our scanner flagged three new packages on npm this week. The packages expresss-validatorr and colorz-utils were published by the same account and run a postinstall script that uploads ~/.npmrc and SSH keys. A third package, react-native-helperz, contained the same payload in version 0.0.2. All three have been reported and removed from the registry.

title: Compromised maintainer account pushes malicious releases of a popular PyPI library
text: Attackers gained access to a maintainer token and published versions 3.4.1 and 3.4.2 of fastjsonlite to PyPI. The malicious releases add a module that downloads a second-stage payload when the package is imported. Version 3.4.0 and earlier are not affected. Users should pin fastjsonlite==3.4.0 and rotate any credentials present on machines that installed the bad versions.

title: Fake AI coding assistant extension on Open VSX
text: An extension named codehelper.claude-assist impersonating an AI coding assistant was listed on Open VSX and installed by Cursor and Windsurf users. Version 2.1.313 of the extension runs a PowerShell command on startup that fetches a remote access trojan. The marketplace removed the listing after our report.

title: Prototype pollution in json-merge-deep
text: A prototype pollution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-41234 and GHSA-abcd-1234-wxyz, affects json-merge-deep before 2.0.5. An attacker who controls an object passed to merge() can modify Object.prototype. Upgrade to 2.0.5.

title: Popular GitHub Action tag rewritten to leak secrets
text: Every release tag of the action tj-files/changed-paths was moved to a commit that prints CI secrets into the workflow log. Workflows that reference the action by tag instead of a full commit SHA ran the malicious code between 14:00 and 21:00 UTC.

title: npm パッケージ mini-logger-jp に悪意のあるコードが混入
text: npm で公開されている mini-logger-jp のバージョン 1.8.0 に、環境変数を外部に送信するコードが含まれていることを確認しました。開発者のアカウントが乗っ取られたとみられます。該当バージョンを利用している場合は 1.7.9 に戻し、認証情報を変更してください。

title: Five habits to harden your CI pipeline
text: Supply-chain attacks keep rising. Pin dependencies by hash, use short-lived credentials, review new maintainers, and enable two-factor authentication on registry accounts. Malicious packages are often discovered within days, so a short cooldown before upgrading helps.

title: Introducing faster dependency review
text: Dependency review now runs twice as fast on large pull requests and shows license information for each changed package. The feature is generally available for all repositories.

title: Weekly security roundup
text: This week was quiet.
